rule: the train with the higher number waits; the lower number overtakes
note: GAPEKA overtakes follow it in 98 % (564; 100 % between train types, 89 % within a type)

rule: a train with CLEARLY higher priority keeps running: KA Dinas yield to regular trains; otherwise the number must be at least priority_number_gap (50) lower; same number: regular before facultative. The direction (odd from the east, even from the west) never decides
note: GAPEKA crossings follow the number in 81 % at gaps >= 100, 73 % at 50-99, 51 % below 50, direction no effect (research/cross_priority.py); first written as plain number order (74 %)

rule: a train with priority never stops at a station it does not serve for a crossing or an overtake (user): where it would reach such a station while the other train is still in the block, the other train is held at its previous station (before the block); at a station where it serves passengers it may wait (more effective, user). Holding the other train is done only when it pays: the delay caused (divided by displace_cost_ratio 3 for trains it clearly outranks) must not exceed the time it gains; otherwise it waits
note: replaces the earlier "first to arrive waits" exception. GAPEKA has 57 crossings where the lower number waits, all at its passenger stops: allowed (user: more effective there); kept as printed. planner.plan_priority: the higher-numbered scheduled train is displaced and re-planned in priority order (it may displace higher numbers in turn); a train created outside the schedule never displaces a scheduled one. Test (research/priority_displace.py, the 57 stations treated as not served): lower number waits there 39 -> 1; displaced trains end median 11 min later than GAPEKA (45 % within 5 min)

rule: equal numbers (e.g. 2501 / 2501F): the regular train before the facultative one
note: not tested (no data)

rule: real GAPEKA trains keep who waits as printed (remarks x / = / //) and their printed times
note: the priority rule is only for trains the simulator plans itself

rule: a train longer than the station's Roman tracks can still be crossed: it departs first; the other train must stop and fit a track (or the two use non-adjacent tracks)
note: track lengths: infra.db station_tracks; train length: gapeka.db consists. GAPEKA: Rogojampi / Temuguruh / Singosari waits by long trains all follow it (research/layout_checks.py)

rule: every train involved in an overtake must fit the track it stands on (effective length)
note: special cases ignored (user)

rule: trains standing at a station at the same time never exceed its Roman (main + siding) tracks; Arabic-numbered tracks are stabling / yard only
note: GAPEKA: 296 stations checked, no exceedance except two diagrams read only in part (research/layout_checks.py)

rule: at a double / single track transition a train waiting on its own running track from the double-track side does not need to fit (its rear stands on the double track); the other train runs through on the other track
note: e.g. Cikadongdong: the stopping train waits on II, the through train runs on III

rule: a train standing at a station while no other train is there or passes need not fit a siding (it may stand on the main track)
note: e.g. 338F stops at Telawa 07:16-07:18 alone, longer than every Telawa track: allowed. The fit rules apply only while another train is at / through the station

rule: a train standing at a station that is longer than every Roman track there blocks the station entry: the whole station counts as occupied; no other train may enter or pass until it has departed (trains already standing there in a track they fit may stay and leave after it); followers wait at the previous station and are released to arrive when the long train is projected to have departed (as the release rule)
note: research/blocked_station.py: 106 such stops (GD wagon 12.5 m): 91 follow it (5 with a train already inside); all passenger cases follow it; the 15 exceptions all involve freight whose length is uncertain (SF may be the maximum consist), e.g. Telawa 2713 / 54, Kalisetail 2763F / 2764F, Lawang / Singosari / Sengon tankers

rule: freight already scheduled in GAPEKA is tolerated where it breaks the fit / blocked-station rules (rules/fit_exemptions.csv: the printed cases); the rules stay strict for new trains and for any train whose times the user changes at that station
note: SF looks like the real formation (news: KA Ronggo 25 GD = SF 25), so these cases are not explained by shorter consists; 15 cases at Gundih, Kalibaru, Kedungjati, Kalisetail, Lawang, Singosari, Sengon, Tanggung, Telawa

rule: trains arriving from the marked side are not held at the entry signal (station_signal_marks: entry signal on a gradient > 8 permil); plan the wait at the previous station or let the train in
note: icon at the diagram end: 'kelandaian sinyal masuk lebih dari 8 permil, tidak perlu mempertahankan sinyal masuk pada semboyan 7' (user); 54 station ends on the sheets, every one with a known gradient faces 10-40 permil (Nagreg, Garut line, Cipeundeuy, Tasikmalaya-Banjar, Sukabumi line, Bumiayu, Ketapang-Kalisat-Klakah)

rule: when the next station has no free usable track: do not hold the train until a train has left there; release it so it ARRIVES when a track usable in its direction and long enough becomes free (departure = track free time - running time + dispatcher gap; never before its own stop / crossing / overtake constraints here); on single track the section must also stay free; strict where the next entry signal has a > 8 permil mark (no holding at that signal)
note: just-in-time release instead of waiting for the next station's departure (user). GAPEKA 2026 (research/release_timing.py): 529 cases with the next station full in the train's direction, 528 KRL on double track; never held until the train ahead left; released 1 min (10 cases 2 min) before the train ahead leaves the next station, arriving ~4 min (median) after the track frees, never before. Default release offset 1 min before that departure; the 'arrive when free' timing is the earliest allowed

rule: the margin exists to protect the follower's path BEYOND the next station (not blocked by the train ahead at the station after): follower continuing on the same path -> leave the previous station no later than 1 min before the train ahead leaves the next station; follower ending at the next station or leaving it on another route -> no onward margin (arrive when a track is free); long blocks after the next station -> larger margin so the follower is not stopped at the following station (from the running time through that block)
note: GAPEKA 2026 (research/release_timing.py): same path 517 cases 1 min (5 x 2 min); other route 11 cases and terminating 1 case also 1-2 min, but whole-minute times hide anything below 1 min and these groups are small; section length after the next station (0-2 / 2-3 / 3-5 / >5 km) does not change the margin on the KRL lines (short automatic blocks everywhere)

rule: during the closed period the closed stations are ignored in scheduling (user): no crossing, overtaking or block point there; the piece between the two open boundary stations (stasiun batas) is one block section: a train must pass all closed stations and reach the next open station before the section is declared clear for the next train (either direction); trains run through on the straight main track; a closed station may still be a passenger stop (like a halt, no staff)
source: manual (user) + PD 19 Jilid I Bab VI (Pasal 97-108; web excerpts) + GAPEKA marks
note: GAPEKA 2026: 271 runs through pieces while closed, never two trains between the boundary stations at once; 0 of 76 crossings / overtakes at closable stations in a closed window; local trains (442-461, 507-510) stop at closed stations

rule: a station that should close but still has a train to handle stays open as stasiun batas luar biasa and splits the piece; a piece can be shortened / lengthened by order (PPK / Wam); an extra train (KLB) through a closed piece is decided in advance (Daop, Direksi between regions), at the latest on the open day before the closure
note: simulator: a delayed train crossing into the closed period keeps its stations open; a new train in a closed piece is allowed only as a planned KLB (warn otherwise)

rule: change from dinas tutup to dinas buka: the boundary stations must have finished the block / train-report exchange for the last train of the closed period, or the closed-period equipment must be switched over and the links to the open stations on both sides working, at the latest 10 min before the first train of the open period (end time set by the operations order from GAPEKA, Pasal 99-100); a delay that moves the change is logged by the boundary PPKA / PAP
note: GAPEKA 2026: last closed pass -> first open train at each closable station 21-133 min (all >= 10); simulator: a closed station is open for a train only if it opened >= 10 min before it

rule: warn when the trains per day over a section exceed its capacity K (infra.db section_capacity); load = trains counted from the timetable along the section's station path (timetable_regular + timetable_facultative) plus user-added trains
applies_to: never the printed P (secondary data); the section can still take trains but they meet more hurdles because scheduled trains keep priority
note: manual (user) + PDF pages 1866-1874
column6: P = program (scheduled trains a/b = regular / facultative), K = capacity per day; busiest: Pasarsenen - Jatinegara 349 of 354, Klari - Cikampek 208 of 224; no section over K in GAPEKA 2026

rule: trains of EQUAL priority (numbers less than priority_number_gap = 50 apart, same kind): neither has the right of way; the crossing goes where the total delay of both trains is least (holding the other train counts its delay in full)
note: user: a 1-number difference must not decide priority, nor the direction; GAPEKA: numbers < 50 apart follow the number only 51 % (chance)
